headline: Rival party colours as a rainbow, a break hidden in code and a deal with the wrong GTA

campaigns.summary: A newspaper front page arranged rival political parties' colours into a rainbow to call for repeal of a law used against gay people.
campaigns.did: On the International Day for Tolerance, the Beirut daily ran a front page that set the colours of Lebanon's rival political parties side by side as a rainbow, under the line that Article 534 is not natural. The 1943 law has been used to prosecute same-sex relations. Inside, the paper surveyed the parties on repeal and carried LGBT citizens' own accounts.
campaigns.why: It turned symbols that usually mark division into one shared image, and used a paper's own front page as the medium. Israel National News called it a striking intervention for a major Arabic-language daily. No measured results are out yet.
campaigns.steal: Take the visual codes of groups who never agree and combine them into one image that makes your point. Use a channel you already own as the stage, rather than buying space.

campaigns.summary: A prompt for AI coding assistants counts every equals sign a developer generates and prompts a break once enough pile up.
campaigns.did: Developers copy a prompt from a microsite into their AI coding assistant. It runs alongside the session and counts the equals signs in the code, since two parallel lines look like two KitKat fingers. At set thresholds a break reminder appears, and at the final one the developer gets a GrabMart voucher for KitKat.
campaigns.why: The insight is that fast AI code removes the natural pauses in a coder's day. The brand line arrives inside the work instead of beside it. B&T, Marketing-Interactive and WeRSM covered it; no results are out yet.
campaigns.steal: Find a symbol or action your audience repeats all day and make it trigger your brand moment. Deliver a small utility through a tool people already use, so there is nothing new to install.

campaigns.summary: An optician teased a huge GTA partnership as the game launched, then revealed it had sponsored a haulage firm with the same initials.
campaigns.did: As GTA VI arrived, Specsavers announced its biggest partnership of all time with GTA. The partner turned out to be GTA Transport Ltd, a haulage firm in Leicester. The brand's sponsorships lead said a deal is a deal and offered every GTA Transport driver a free eye test.
campaigns.why: The mix-up acts out the brand's long-running line about people who should have gone to Specsavers, so the joke needs no explaining. Creative Bloq called it a rare exception to lazy trendjacking, and Mediaweek reported commenters praising the stunt.
campaigns.steal: When everyone chases the same moment, find a smaller namesake and make the mistake the story. It works best when the joke proves your existing slogan.
